diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\item $\alpha$ is a Poisson map,
        \item $\beta$ is an anti-Poisson map,

issues.failure_explanation: Applying the paper's own order-4 Karasev truncation (eq: approximation alpha) to the paper's own Poissonization Pi gives, at order 2, alpha^{q^i} = q^i - (1/2t)xi_{p_i}, alpha^{p_i} = p_i + (1/2t)(xi_{q^i}+p_i xi_z), alpha^z = z - (1/2)(p_i xi_{p_i}/t - xi_t), alpha^t = t - xi_z/2, because Pi^{q^i p_j} = -delta^i_j/t, Pi^{p_i z} = p_i/t, Pi^{z p_j} = -p_j/t, Pi^{zt} = 1. The displayed alpha equals the correct beta and the displayed beta equals the correct alpha: the two maps are interchanged (equivalently, the signs of the xi-dependent terms in alpha are flipped). Consequently the displayed alpha is anti-Poisson and the displayed beta is Poisson, so the example does not satisfy the bi-realization axioms (alpha Poisson, beta anti-Poisson) for the stated Poisson manifold (P_J, Pi).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Interchange the alpha and beta formulas (equivalently, flip the signs of the xi-dependent terms in alpha) so that alpha agrees with the truncation of tau composed with the half-time spray flow given by eq: approximation alpha applied to the stated Pi; beta then follows from the Karasev property beta(x,xi) = alpha(x,-xi).
issues.overall_effect: The paper's only explicit homogeneous bi-realization example (eq: bi-realization example, eq: bi-realization example2) is wrong as stated: it realizes the Poisson structure with flipped signs rather than the Poissonization of the contact structure under consideration. No labelled result depends on the example.
issues.title: Sign error in the order-2 Karasev approximation: alpha and beta are interchanged
issues.why_classification: The error is confined to an illustrative example; the repair is a local sign flip (or label interchange) forced by the paper's own formula and Poisson structure, with no loss of any guarantee and no dependent result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We call exact a smooth family of Lagrangian submanifolds $(L_s)_{s\in I}$ such that its corresponding variation $1$-forms $(\xi_s)_{s\in I}$ are exact; in that case we call variation functions to any time-dependent functions $(f_s)_{s\in I}$ such that $df_s = \xi_s$, for all $s\in I$.

issues.failure_explanation: Variation functions are only determined up to additive constants. The 'if' direction is false: df_s 1-homogeneous does not imply f_s 1-homogeneous. For instance, the constant function f_s = 1 has df_s = 0 (which is 1-homogeneous) but is not 1-homogeneous. What is true is that 1-homogeneous variation functions can always be chosen (by fixing the constants), i.e. f_s is 1-homogeneous up to an additive constant.

failure_location.quote: Then $\xi_s$ are $1$-homogeneous if and only if $f_s$ are $1$-homogeneous.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add 'up to an additive constant' (equivalently: 1-homogeneous variation functions can always be chosen); no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary as stated is false; the construction narrative, which needs 1-homogeneous variation functions to obtain homogeneous integrators, is unaffected once the statement is repaired to 'up to an additive constant'.
issues.title: Converse direction of the homogeneity corollary for variation functions is false
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line qualification; the substantive content (existence of 1-homogeneous variation functions) survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There is an equivalence of categories between the Jacobi (resp. contact) category and the homogeneous Poisson (resp. symplectic) category.
A smooth family of homogeneous diffeomorphisms of $P$, $(\phi_\epsilon)_\epsilon$ is a homogeneous Poisson Hamilton integrator of order $k\geq 1$ for $H^P$ if:
A smooth family of diffeomorphisms of $J$, $(\phi_\epsilon)_\epsilon$ is a  Jacobi Hamiltonian integrator of order $k\geq 1$ for $H^J$ if:

issues.failure_explanation: The cited equivalence of categories yields only a correspondence of objects (Jacobi vs homogeneous Poisson manifolds) and morphisms (Jacobi vs homogeneous Poisson diffeomorphisms). The integrator correspondence additionally requires: (i) homogeneous diffeomorphisms of P_J descend to Jacobi diffeomorphisms of J = P_J/R^x; (ii) a 1-homogeneous time-dependent Hamiltonian on P_J descends to a Jacobi Hamiltonian on J and the flow of the lifted Hamiltonian projects to the flow of the descended one (because the lifted Hamiltonian vector field is tau-related to the Jacobi Hamiltonian vector field of the descended function); (iii) the order condition H_s = H + o(s^{k-1}) is preserved under descent. None of this is argued in the source; the claim is true but unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: Using the equivalence between the Jacobi category and homogeneous Poisson category (Proposition \ref{Prop-equiv-cat}), we can conclude that we have a $1$-to-$1$ correspondence between homogeneous Poisson Hamiltonian integrators and Jacobi Hamiltonian integrators. This grants the existence of JHI's, constructed as explained above.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the descent/lift argument: homogeneous Poisson diffeomorphisms of P_J descend to Jacobi diffeomorphisms of J; 1-homogeneous Hamiltonians descend to Jacobi Hamiltonians (evaluated at t=1) preserving the o(s^{k-1}) condition; and the flows correspond since the lifted and Jacobi Hamiltonian vector fields are tau-related.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central existence claim for Jacobi Hamiltonian integrators rests on a justification that does not cover the order conditions, the time-dependent Hamiltonians, or the projection of flows; as written, the existence of JHI's is not established by the cited result.
issues.title: Existence of JHI's and the hPHI-JHI correspondence are asserted without the required descent argument
issues.why_classification: The claim is true and the missing argument is a short, routine computation; no new construction is needed and no scope or guarantee is lost, though the central claim is currently under-supported.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We want to prove that $\pi_*(h_z^*(\alpha)) = h_z^*(\pi_*(\alpha)).$
If $N$ is a point, then we can find a contractible neighborhood of $N$, and $\beta$ is given by the homogeneous Poincar\'e Lemma.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only establishes that the fiber operator pi_* commutes with h_z^* for 1-homogeneous forms on U x [0,1]; it never introduces a homotopy, never proves that a closed 1-homogeneous form is exact, and never identifies a primitive (homogeneous or not). The lemma's main assertion is therefore unproved. Moreover, the statement (homogeneous star-shaped subsets of R^n with the linear action) does not match its application in the proof of thm:added-1: a contractible neighborhood of a point in a homogeneous manifold is not invariant under the free R^x-action, so it is not a 'homogeneous star-shaped subset of R^n'.

failure_location.quote: Let $U$ be a homogeneous star-shaped open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$, then all $1$-homogeneous closed $p$-forms are exact and their primitive is also homogeneous.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the standard homotopy argument: introduce H(x,t) = tx, the homotopy operator I(omega) = integral_0^1 H_t^*(i_{d/dt H} omega) dt, show omega = d(I(omega)) for closed 1-homogeneous omega (using H_0^* omega = 0 and H_1 = id), and deduce 1-homogeneity of the primitive from the commutation already proved; restate the lemma for invariant cone neighborhoods to cover the application.
issues.overall_effect: The homogeneous Poincare Lemma is unproved as written; its use in the proof of the homogeneous Darboux-Weinstein theorem (thm:added-1, case where N is a point) is affected. The lemma is standard and true, so no downstream statement is lost.
issues.title: Proof of the homogeneous Poincare Lemma never proves exactness
issues.why_classification: The proof as written never addresses the lemma's main claim (exactness); completing it requires inserting the standard homotopy argument - a missing nontrivial step - and adjusting the statement to cover its application, although the lemma and all its uses survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then we can find a time-dependent vector field $\eta_s$ such that $i_{\eta_s}\omega_s = \beta$.

issues.failure_explanation: The straight-line family need not be symplectic even in the homogeneous setting: on T*R^2 with coordinates (q_i, xi_i), the 1-homogeneous action h_z(q,xi) = (q, z xi), and N the zero section, take omega_0 = dq_1 wedge dxi_1 + dq_2 wedge dxi_2 and omega_1 = dq_1 wedge dxi_1 - dq_2 wedge dxi_2 + 2 dq_1 wedge dxi_2. Both are 1-homogeneous symplectic and agree on N (both restrict to 0), but omega_{1/2} = dq_1 wedge dxi_1 + dq_1 wedge dxi_2 is degenerate (dq_1 wedge dxi_2 terms give zero top power). Hence the Moser step (solving i_{eta_s} omega_s = beta and integrating) is unjustified as written.

failure_location.quote: Since $\omega_s|_X$ is symplectic for all $s\in[0,1]$, this is true for a small neighborhood of $N$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the straight-line family by a path of symplectic forms agreeing on N (whose existence is a nontrivial linear-algebra fact) and run the Moser trick along it, or otherwise supply a correct proof of the theorem; the statement is unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the homogeneous Darboux-Weinstein theorem has a defective central step; the theorem's statement survives (it is classical and true), and in the application inside the proof of the homogeneous Weinstein Lagrangian theorem (thm:added-2) the two forms agree on all of TM|_X, where the straight-line family is nondegenerate, so that application is not affected.
issues.title: False nondegeneracy claim for the straight-line family in the homogeneous Darboux-Weinstein proof
issues.why_classification: The central Moser step rests on a false claim (explicit counterexample); the theorem is true so no result is lost, but repairing the proof requires a genuinely different argument - the crux of the classical Darboux-Weinstein theorem - not a local fix.
